answer: At the Linnet Ropewalk, six ghost crews cloned a shift token and took the 05:05 laying slot. To claim it, a foreman walks the 280 m shed, hitches a 21 m yarn to the south capstan anchor, runs 12 minutes of live twist at 14 rpm, and cuts a 40 cm witness with that hour's lot punch. Only yarn that took 168 live turns keeps a 3.2 mm helical set a spare cannot fake. He logs the pitch against the 05:17 transit of comet 12P and presses the tag into the still-wet ochre daybook, boiled that morning from local yarrow. A missing helix or skinned ochre cancels the lay and forfeits the week's deposit.
